audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 read Skill and the two-item row read Riven, the latter directly contradicting its own why ('Your 2+ item AP scaling and pool disengage flip it to Vladimir').
audit.why: The mirror audit (riven__vladimir) set Level 6 to Riven and two-plus items to Vladimir. Riven's level-6 spike hands her AD, range and a Wind Slash while Hemoplague is a delayed zone, so six is hers; the scaling row belongs to Vladimir, which is the only reason a 47.27% lane is playable at all.
audit.corrected: Rows 4 and 6 flipped in phases[N].side and win[N] as one paired atomic group with ratings, and whys[4] rewritten to match.

audit.why: Riven spikes at level 3, level 6 and first item; Vladimir's is two items. Spike timings already correct.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text calls Wind Slash an 'execute' and the late text says it 'executes your empowered pool state'.
audit.why: Riot's R text says Blade of the Exile grants Attack Damage and Range and lets her use Wind Slash, a powerful ranged attack, once. There is no execute in the text and the kit carries no execute flag — the mirror reached the same conclusion. Treating it as a threshold kill changes how a player fights at low health, so the wrong word here is genuinely dangerous. What is real: it is one shot per ult, it is a projectile, and Ki Burst is 11s at rank 1 while Sanguine Pool is 28s at rank 1 for 2 seconds of untargetable — so the pool has to be spent on the stun, not on the ult.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text rewritten to describe the ult accurately and to keep the pool assigned to Ki Burst; dontsFull[1].d now says the same in the don'ts.
